approachQuestion.prompt: Evaluate a valid expression of nonnegative integer literals, +, -, *, and parentheses. * has higher precedence than + and -, and equal-precedence operators associate left to right. There are no unary operators; subtraction is binary. Length<=200,000; every intermediate result fits signed 64-bit. Example "8-(2-3)*4" -> 12; "2+3*4" -> 14. Literals are decimal digits representing values from 0 to 1,000,000,000, with no whitespace. Let n be the character count; reading all digits counts toward processing time. Return one signed integer.

options.text: Use value and operator stacks. Push operators by precedence, reducing higher/equal precedence first; reduce through the matching opening parenthesis at close, then reduce remaining operators.
options.feedback: The operator stack preserves grouping and precedence while the value stack holds completed operands.

options.text: Evaluate strictly left to right, applying every binary operator as it appears.
options.feedback: This ignores precedence: 2+3*4 would become 20 instead of 14.

options.text: Split at each plus sign and sum the resulting integer tokens.
options.feedback: This loses subtraction, multiplication, and parenthesized grouping; 8-(2-3)*4 evaluates to 12.

options.text: Recursively parse using precedence into an expression tree and evaluate that tree in postorder.
options.feedback: Each token and expression node is processed once; the expression tree and recursive frames have linear worst-case size, tying the two-stack method.

feedback.reason: For 1-(2-3)*4, the parenthesized value is -1, then multiplied by 4 and subtracted, yielding 5.
details: Use value and operator stacks. Push operators by precedence, reducing higher/equal precedence first; reduce through the matching opening parenthesis at close, then reduce remaining operators.

Reduce higher-precedence operators before lower-precedence ones, and equal-precedence ones in their stated associativity order. Pop right operand before left. Parentheses delimit reductions rather than contributing numeric values.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For infix-arithmetic-evaluation-optimal, let n be the number of input operations or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: The input is immutable; returned output is excluded from auxiliary space. All stack operations and value comparisons take constant time.
The algorithm is iterative with O(1) call-stack use. The auxiliary stack may hold up to n fixed-size entries.
No hashing, recursion, or hidden array copy occurs. Any movement between stacks counts as constant time per item.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Digits are scanned once and each operator is pushed and reduced once.
details: Each digit is scanned once; each operator is pushed and reduced once. An arbitrarily nested valid expression retains a linear number of operators and pending values. Fixed-size arithmetic is constant time by the range guarantee. Thus total time and working space are O(n); the scalar result is excluded.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested expressions retain pending operators and values along a linear-depth chain, independent of the scalar result.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each digit is read once and each operator is reduced once; precedence reduction consumes saved state rather than reparsing prefixes.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A final operand can change the numeric result, so the worst case reads the whole expression.
